label: L-02
title: Once phUSD and the minter are both wired, the phUSD address can never be changed - the two setters mutually lock
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.

classification.assetImpact: No funds at risk. A phUSD redeployment would force a full Antimatter redeployment, losing all antimatter balances (non-upgradeable, no migration path).
attackPath: 1. Owner wires phUSD and the minter.

2. setPhUSD refuses any address the configured minter does not mint; setPhUSDMinter refuses any minter that does not mint the configured phUSD; PhusdStableMinter.phUSD is immutable; neither setter accepts address(0) to unwire.
3. No ordering of calls reaches a different phUSD. The pair is permanently welded.
classification.likelihood: Low frequency, but certain if a phUSD migration is ever needed.
classification.assumptions: phUSD is intended to be permanent, which is why this is Low rather than Medium.

justification: Low, Law-3 footgun. An owner reading two independent setters would reasonably believe either can be re-pointed; discovering the weld only at the moment a migration is needed is a surprise with an expensive remedy - so it is in scope rather than suppressed as centralization. Not Medium: no funds at risk, and the permanence is consistent with intent.
recommendation: Document the one-way property on setPhUSD, or add an owner-only `rewire(IFlax newPhUSD, PhusdStableMinter newMinter)` that sets both atomically and re-checks consistency - preserving the no-drift invariant without welding the pair.

No ordering of calls reaches a different phUSD, and neither setter accepts address(0) to unwire.
